Subject: Dedicated capacity request — Nimbus AI pilot

Hi Soojin / Marissa,

Thanks for taking this — we're aiming to run a Q3 pilot of our conversational agent on dedicated capacity. Short summary:
- Model: nimbus-lm-13B (decoder-only)
- Expected peak concurrency: 220 rps (50 token requests avg, 1k token tail occasionally)
- Context window: 32k tokens (we'll use KV cache heavily for long chat histories)
- Latency SLO: 250ms p95 on short-turns (~50 tokens)
- Security: VPC + customer-managed KMS

Can you share a sizing estimate that maps model/context/config to GPU counts and a short note on how quantization would change capacity needs? I've attached our request spreadsheet (nimbus-dedicated-reqs.xlsx). Also looped in procurement (Tina) for timing.

Thanks — happy to jump on a 30m sync if helpful.

—Harper
Director of Product, Nimbus AI

Harper — thanks for the details and the spreadsheet. Quick clarifying questions before we run a formal capacity model:
- When you say 220 rps peak, is that steady-state concurrency or short bursts?
- For the 1k-token tails, what fraction of requests do you expect to exceed 512/2048 tokens? (ballpark % is fine)
- Will you accept an initial canary with 8xA100-80GB equiv (FP16) and then a follow-up reserved pool once performance is validated?

Preliminary guidance:
- Model footprint (13B) baseline FP16: ~28–32GB host+GPU memory for weights loaded (sharded). With 32k KV cache, expect ~12–16GB additional GPU-side KV for large sequence windows depending on KV offload policy.
- Quantization: moving to 4-bit Q4_* can reduce weight memory ~2–2.5x; however KV cache doesn't quantize the same way — KV is dense and largely unaffected unless we use lossy compression which impacts quality.

I'll run a workload-specific estimate (sheets attached) and include GPU counts for three fidelity lanes: FP16, 8-bit quant (SymInt8), and 4-bit quant (Q4_*).

Proposed next step: 30m technical sync (this week) — I'll include Marissa (inference optimization) and Jonas (distro/ops) to capture deployment constraints.

—So (Sojin)
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Harper / Tina — looping in commercial context. A couple of items from our side:
- Commercial cadence: pilots typically run 6–8 weeks with a conversion path to reserved capacity. We can structure a pilot discount and commit to ramp timing in the SOW.
- If Nimbus wants dedicated hardware with burst capacity, we'll provision a mixed pool: hot nodes for low-latency and cheaper cold nodes for background jobs.

Rough capacity estimate (very high level, subject to Marissa's engineering sizing):
- FP16 (baseline): ~12 x A100-80GB equiv to meet 220 rps with 32k KV and p95 latency target, assuming batching and prefix caching.
- SymInt8 (~8-bit quant): ~9 x A100-80GB equiv (weights smaller -> more models per GPU; KV unchanged).
- Q4_* (aggressive 4-bit): ~6–7 x A100-80GB equiv (strongest reduction in weight memory, still need KV budget on GPU or with offload).

Commercial ask: if we show a 6–7 GPU point for Q4, we can tie a pricing band to the quantization profile chosen in the SOW. Also confirming procurement window and any SOC2 evidence they need — Tina?

—Ben
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity request — Nimbus AI pilot

Hi team — dug into the attached sheet and ran micro-simulations against the nimbus-lm-13B profile. High-level technical sizing and operational notes:

Key assumptions I used:
- Serving config: dynamic KV cache pinned to GPU for best latency on 32k windows (we tested -> GPU-pin gives ~40–70ms savings p95 vs host-offload for frequent revisits).
- Batch sizing: avg effective batch size 6 for short-turns, up to 12 for long tails where latency is looser.
- Perf profile taken from Redwood benchmark harness (similar architecture 13B).

Estimated GPU memory usage per model instance:
- FP16 weights (sharded) + activations: ~30GB
- KV cache for active 32k context (pinned): ~14GB (sensitive to tokenization and kv datatype)
- Overheads (tracing, runtime): ~2–4GB
- Total per model instance (FP16): ~46–48GB

For an A100-80GB equiv node we can safely consolidate 1 model instance per GPU when KV pinned. If we accept KV host-offload (with async prefetch) we can fit up to 2 instances per GPU but p95 jumps ~1.7x.

Quantization impact (measured):
- SymInt8: weight memory drops ~1.9x -> weights ~16GB, total per instance ~32–34GB -> ~2 instances per A100-80GB w/ limited KV pinning (trade: slightly higher latency variability).
- Q4_*: weights ~8–9GB, total per instance ~24–26GB -> up to 3 instances per GPU if KV offload is acceptable; with GPU-pinned KV expect 1–2 instances depending on exact KV footprint.

Operational recommendation for pilot:
1) Canary phase (2 weeks): 4 GPUs FP16 pinned KV (validate latency and cache hit rates).
2) Pilot scale (6–8 weeks): 8 GPUs FP16 (target safe headroom) with autoscale policy to burst additional 4 GPUs in quantized band if accuracy allows.
3) If Nimbus elects Q4_* in SOW after validation, commit to reserved 6–7 GPUs for steady-state.

Notes on risk:
- Aggressive quantization can reduce cost materially but requires evals on your prompt sets — accuracy regressions are possible for long-context retrievals.
- KV offload saves GPU memory but increases p95 significantly for hot-prefix patterns.

Attachments: I exported the per-turn memory trace to memory-svc-estimate.csv and a short model profile (nimbus-model-profile.pdf). Happy to review these numbers on the sync — I can change assumptions on host-offload latency and re-run.

—Marissa
Principal Applied ML Engineer, Redwood Inference
